newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker in moderate trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker in moderate trading.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker on Wednesday at C$1.3677 (US$0.7311) from Tuesday's close of C$1.3667 (US$0.7316) in moderate trading, dealers said.
* They said the currency gave back some of its recent gains after the release of encouraging U.S. data showed a narrowing trade gap.
U.S. imports grew a more modest 1.2 percent to a record US$84.99 billion. They were kept in check by the lower value of imported cars and parts, primarily from Canada.
Traders said Canada's dollar opened stronger on Wednesday at C$1.3626 (US$0.7338) in light trading after rallying on Tuesday news the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady.

The Canadian dollar had been under pressure from investors since the Federal Reserve raised interest rates on March 25 and the Bank of Canada held its own rates steady. On the crosses, Canada's dollar rose to 83.37 yen from Tuesday's close of 82.34 yen and jumped to 1.2345 marks from 1.2263 marks.
